newsitem.title: ITALY: Zaire says ready to help U.N. relief effort.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says ready to help U.N. relief effort.

text.p: Zaire told U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Monday that it was willing to help the United Nations get aid to more than a million refugees in the east of the country, a spokeswoman for Boutros-Ghali said.
Therese Gastaut said in a statement that Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo had made the pledge in a lengthy telephone conversation with Boutros-Ghali, who is in Rome for the World Food Summit.
It said they discussed "the urgent need to provide humanitarian assistance to refugees and others displaced by the conflict in Eastern Zaire."
The wording of the statement appeared to cover both Rwandan and Burundian refugees and internally-displaced Zaireans.

The statement said Boutros-Ghali continued to believe that a multinational force was needed to create the conditions for a humanitarian operation in eastern Zaire, where Tutsi rebels are fighting Zairean troops backed by Rwandan Hutu hardliners.
The violence has put at risk more than a million refugees from previous bloodletting in Rwanda and Burundi.

"The Secretary-General said there had been a positive exchange of views, with (Kengo) declaring his willingness to cooperate with the United Nations to facilitate the provision of humanitarian assistance," the statement said.

It said the U.N. Coordinator of Humanitarian Assistance for the Great Lakes Region, Sergio Vieira de Mello, who is in Kinshasa, would meet senior Zairean officials to arrange details of delivering aid to eastern Zaire.

"The Secretary-General hopes these efforts will bring quick results but recognises that the extreme security situation demands a multinational force in the region to create conditions for a humanitarian operation," the statement said.
Foreign relief workers took some aid into the eastern Zairean city of Goma on Monday, but refugees remained beyond reach and were reported to be dying in their thousands.

Vehicles and workers from the U.N. Children's Fund, Concern, Save the Children, Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF-Doctors without Frontiers), CARE and the British agency Merlin drove into Goma from Rwanda, aid officials said.
The last foreign aid workers in eastern Zaire were evacuated from Goma more than a week ago in a lull in battles for the city.
The Rwandan government on Sunday gave the go ahead for some aid to reach eastern Zaire from its territory but still wants the bulk of aid to come to Rwanda in a bid to coax the refugees to come home.
